caption:
The IPO price isn't the price most people pay. 🧠

The night before a company lists, it and its banks set the offer price, and most shares go to big investors who already asked for them. Next morning, the exchange runs an auction. The price where the most shares can trade becomes the opening price. That gap is the IPO pop.

The one-liner: the offer price is a negotiation. The opening price is an auction.

$20 and $28 are illustrative. The 20% / 11% figures are from a study of Nasdaq IPOs (Aggarwal & Wu). Not financial advice.
